title: Hosted API upgrade sequencer: tenant-aware traffic failsafe and staged version pinning
creator: Avery Chen
description: Problem: Our current hosted-API rollout logic is region-weighted and lacks tenant-level affinity and explicit LTS pinning. This causes noisy upgrades for large tenants and prevents controlled rollbacks per customer. Goal: Implement an 'Upgrade Sequencer' service that orchestrates tenant-aware staged upgrades, enforces LTS channel pinning, supports soft-launch traffic mirroring/shadowing, and exposes SLO-driven rollout gates and automatic rollback windows. The sequencer will act as the canonical decision point for any non-trivial deployment (blue/green or canary) and integrate with Smart Router, Console rollouts, and Autoscaler. Constraints: minimal latency impact on the request path, backwards-compatible with existing routing fallbacks, support for per-tenant opt-outs, and clear audit trail for compliance.
acceptance_criteria: Upgrade Sequencer runs as a distinct control-plane service with authentication and RBAC
Operators can create an upgrade plan that lists target version, LTS channel, tenant scope (single tenant / tenant cohort / global), and schedule
Traffic routing supports these modes: mirror (0%), canary (configurable weight), staged ramp (time or SLO-based), full cutover
SLO gates: error-rate, p95 latency, token-rate, and model-quality regression signals can pause/rollback automatically
Sequencer exposes audit log of decisions and per-tenant event stream for Console and compliance export
Automatic rollback triggers within 15 minutes of breach and manual operator override available in Console
Integration tests validate sequencer behavior end-to-end with simulated SLO breaches and tenant-scoped rollbacks
implementation_plan: Design API surface: create /upgrade-plans, /plans/{id}/actions (start/pause/abort/status) with version and lts_channel fields
Schema for tenant scoping: single tenant IDs, tag-based cohorts, or percentage segments
Traffic controller hooks: extend Smart Router to accept sequencer-provided weights and shadow rules via a lightweight token map
State and durability: store plans and history in the configDB with change events sent to Kafka topics for eventual consistency with Console and observability pipelines
Gate evaluations: wire SLO signals (Prometheus, tracing, quality-eval) into gate engine; implement threshold config and cooldown windows
Operator UI: Console page for plans with timeline visualization, per-tenant status, and one-click rollback
Canary policy library: common policies (time-based ramp, traffic-percent ramp, error-rate quickstop) as reusable templates
End-to-end tests: local harness and sandbox runbook to simulate global rollout and selective tenant rollback
monitoring_and_rollbacks: Primary metrics: per-tenant requests/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency, 5xx rate, model-quality delta for eval prompts
Gate thresholds (initial): p95 latency +25% over baseline OR 5xx spike > 3x baseline for 5 minutes -> pause; for customers with SLA flagged as high, threshold tightened by 30%
Rollback flow: sequencer marks tenant cohort as 'rollback in progress', instructs Smart Router to move traffic to previous version immediately, triggers postmortem flag and creates incident stub
Alerting: playbook channel with runbook link, automated Slack alert with plan id and breach reason, Console banner for affected tenants
Observability: plan-level dashboard, per-tenant timeline, raw event logs retained for 90 days for compliance
notes: Trade-offs: centralizing decision logic simplifies cross-tenant policies but introduces a single control-plane failure mode; mitigations include HA sequencer (leader-elect) and fail-open policy that falls back to existing weight-based defaults
Performance: sequencer must not be in the hot path for every request — it publishes compact decision artifacts consumed by Smart Router (e.g., per-tenant weight map) to avoid per-request RPCs
Version-safety: require model artifact signature verification and compatibility checks before plan activation to avoid mismatched KV cache expectations
Opt-outs: large customers can opt for manual rollouts (dedicated rollout coordinator) which the sequencer will delegate to when flagged
Compliance: include immutable plan history and signed approvals for enterprise accounts; surface in audit exports
